scope: revert one hunk group at a time on head; run FullyQualifiedName~GeneratedMessagePackFormatterTests (6 tests) and FullyQualifiedName~GeneratedFormatterForExternalTypesTests (7 tests); other suites not run

groups.desc: GeneratorUtilities: hand-written formatter search skips classes marked [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
FormatterTemplate.cs and StringKeyFormatterTemplate.cs emit 'partial class' for user-declared formatters (T4 output)
MessagePackGenerator: collect [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes and add their models
Analyzer SupportedDiagnostics lists the four new descriptors
Constants for the attribute name and SurrogateType (used by h17, h16, h12: structural when alone)
ObjectSerializationInfo.IsUserDeclaredFormatter property (used by templates and collector: structural when alone)
MessagePackGenerator: all three hunks together (collection, model loop, diagnostics)

not_xrayed.why: Attributes.cs: the new attribute class. Reverting it breaks every project that uses it, so it is structural by construction.
Diagnostic ids and descriptors, used by the collector (h12). Structural when reverted alone.
New files GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs and GeneratedFormatterRequest.cs: removing them removes the feature, and the generator no longer builds.
README, analyzer docs and release notes: no test can fail when documentation is reverted.
.tt template sources are only compiled by T4 outside this build; their .cs outputs (h20, h22) were X-Rayed as g3.
Tests and fixtures: the evidence, not the subject. Time Machine covers them.

order_note: g1 to g8 first run, g3 and g4 reclassified from saved logs after the classifier fix (a compile error only in the test project means the tests notice the revert); g9 run afterwards.
